- Fix a feature-mismatch error at prediction time (e.g., missing `recent_form_diff`, `power_rating_diff`) by making prediction input columns identical to the training schema. 
- Ensure training and runtime prediction always use the same ordered feature list so calibrated models/isotonic calibration do not fail due to missing or reordered columns.

- Updated `predict_runtime` in `main.py` to use `FEATURE_COLUMNS = getattr(runtime_model, "feature_columns", NBA_RUNTIME_FEATURE_COLUMNS)` as the canonical feature list.

- When a `scaler` is present, reconstructed a `DataFrame` after `scaler.transform` using `FEATURE_COLUMNS` to preserve feature names for downstream `predict_proba`. 
- Removed the prior conversion path that could produce unnamed/positional columns before inference and replaced it with a final guarded `reindex` right before `predict_proba`.

### 🎯 Impact
The application was directly interpolating user-controlled variables (such as guest name, event title, comment, and description) into HTML email templates (`src/lib/email-service.ts`) without proper escaping. This created an HTML injection/XSS vulnerability where a malicious user could insert arbitrary HTML tags or scripts into the email payload, potentially affecting the email client of the host or other guests receiving updates.

### 🛡️ Fix
Imported the `escapeHTML` utility from `src/lib/security.ts` and applied it to all user-controlled variables (e.g., `guestName`, `eventTitle`, `comment`, `location`, `description`) within the HTML generation functions (`generateHostNotificationEmailHTML`, `generateReminderEmailHTML`, `generateConfirmationEmailHTML`, `generateUpdateEmailHTML`) before they are embedded into the template strings.

## Summary

Adds a deterministic Wikidata-QID gate inside `suggestUrls()` that drops candidate URLs whose primary subject doesn't match the parent entity. QUA-650's retro-scan caught 76 system-wide verdicts where this pattern hit *after* the fact (e.g. xAI press releases attached to Anthropic funding-rounds); this gate catches the same shape at suggest time, before storage.

Fail-open by design — if either QID is unknown the candidate passes — mirroring the `relevance-gate` / QUA-426 contract. The LLM verify step downstream remains the backstop.

## Changes

- `crux/lib/sourcing/wikidata-matcher.ts` — new `extractQidFromHtml()` so a candidate URL can be checked against pre-fetched HTML (`<link rel>`, `sameAs`, body links).
- `crux/lib/sourcing/subject-identity-gate.ts` (new) — pure gate function; takes any candidate shape with `{ url, html? }`. Accepts a `null` entity QID (full fail-open).
- `crux/lib/sourcing/entity-wikidata-qid.ts` (new) — looks up the parent entity's QID from `data/external-links.yaml`. The ticket's `entities.wikidata` / `wikidata_qid` columns don't actually exist; `external-links.yaml` is the source-of-truth.
- `crux/lib/sourcing/suggest-urls.ts` — accepts `entityWikidataQid`, returns `subjectMismatches[]` for observability. Gate runs after dedup+cap; doesn't backfill from providers (that belongs in the unified pipeline, QUA-722).
- `crux/commands/sourcing-suggest-urls.ts` — looks up the entity's QID per verdict row, plumbs it into `suggestUrls`, prints `[subject-mismatch]` lines and bumps a new `subject_mismatches_dropped` summary counter.

## Acceptance from the ticket

- [x] New gate in `crux/lib/sourcing/suggest-urls.ts`
- [x] Mismatched-QID candidate dropped with `subject-mismatch` reason
- [x] Matching-QID candidate passes

- Retro-sweep over the 76 existing contradicted verdicts → sibling ticket
- Wider entity QID backfill (records without a QID stay fail-open)
- Pre-fetching HTML inside `suggestUrls` itself — that fetch belongs in the unified pipeline (QUA-722) at step 5; the gate accepts pre-fetched HTML via the candidate's optional `html` field

      |        ^~~~
/usr/include/arrow/buffer.h:239:3: note: 'std::span' is only available from C++20 onwards

## Summary

- Adds `repo-analyze-full`, `repo-analyze-quick-full`, and `repo-analyze-strict-full` — full-coverage siblings of the existing repo-analyze skills that dispatch one Sonnet swarm agent per audit section (15 sections, max 5 concurrent agents per wave) so every file is analyzed instead of a sampled subset
- Adds `worktree-cleanup` — audits every git worktree, classifies it into one of five states (`CLEAN_PRUNE_OK` / `NEEDS_COMMIT` / `NEEDS_PUSH` / `NEEDS_PR` / `KEEP`), prunes safe worktrees, and prints exact remediation commands for the rest — never deletes branches (that is `gh tidy`'s exclusive responsibility)
- Updates `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `plugin.json` to register all four new skills

## Design Decisions

- **`-full` variants are separate skill files, not flags** — users who want sampling keep the existing skills; users who want full coverage invoke the `-full` sibling
- **One Sonnet agent per audit section** — 15 sections → 3 waves of 5 agents (respects the Myrmidon swarm 5-concurrent constraint); each agent reads every file in its bucket via `Read` with `offset/limit` chunking if needed
- **`worktree-cleanup` never deletes branches** — branch deletion authority stays exclusively with `gh tidy`; `worktree-cleanup` only runs `git worktree remove` (no `--force`) and defers all destructive ops to the user via printed commands
- **3-method audit pattern** from ProjectMnemosyne `git-worktree-cleanup-preservation-audit` v1.0.0 embedded verbatim: PR state → patch-id (`git cherry`) → tree diff

## Summary

Addresses voog-mcp code-review follow-up **#6**: the `_simplify_pages` and `_simplify_products` functions were byte-identical between `voog_mcp/tools/<group>.py` and `voog_mcp/resources/<group>.py`. The modules' docstrings called the duplication "deliberate", but the same docstrings also promised that callers can't tell which surface produced the data — a contract that a single one-sided typo can silently break.

This PR moves the projections to a single source of truth.

## Changes

- New `voog_mcp/projections.py` exposes `simplify_pages`, `simplify_products`, `simplify_articles`, and `simplify_layouts` — pure stdlib, no MCP/client deps.
- `voog_mcp/tools/pages.py`, `voog_mcp/tools/products.py`, `voog_mcp/resources/pages.py`, `voog_mcp/resources/products.py`, `voog_mcp/resources/articles.py`, `voog_mcp/resources/layouts.py` import from `voog_mcp.projections` instead of carrying their own copy.
- Module docstrings updated — the "deliberately duplicated" notes are gone, replaced with pointers to `projections.py`.
- Articles and layouts only had a single caller (resources side), but the four projections sit together so a future tools-side surface gets the same shape for free.

## Why a contract, not just dedup

The duplicated functions weren't just incidental — they were two implementations of the same promise (the "products_list tool and voog://products resource produce identical shapes" promise from PR #30). With two copies, that promise depended on humans remembering to update both at once. With one source, the promise is structural: the tools-side and resources-side imports are pinned to the exact same callable.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_projections.py` — 16 unit tests covering empty inputs, full inputs, missing fields (graceful `.get()`), extra fields (stripped), and the `layout` nested-fallback precedence in `simplify_pages`.
- The PR #30 cross-module invariant test in `tests/test_tools_products.py` is rewritten: instead of comparing byte-equal outputs of two duplicated functions (which becomes vacuous once both call the same import), it asserts structural identity (`products_tools.simplify_products is projections.simplify_products`) plus a heavy-field-stripping check.
- `tests/test_tools_pages.py`'s two `_simplify_pages` tests now reference the shared `voog_mcp.projections.simplify_pages`.

**409 tests pass** (was 392 — added 16 unit tests in `test_projections.py` plus 1 net-add in `test_tools_products.py`).

author: arxialayer1
body:
# Commit 040 — `arxia-proto::validate_transport_frame_bytes` pre-decode size cap

**Severity:** high
**Bug reference:** PHASE1_AUDIT_REPORT.md ID **HIGH-010**
**Scope:** `crates/arxia-proto/src/{lib.rs, validation.rs}` only.

## Vulnerability

`arxia-proto` exposes prost-generated wire types (TransportFrame,
GossipEnvelope, NonceSync*, Ping, Vote, etc.) but had no
pre-decode size validation. The audit (HIGH-010):

> **Attack:** send a 4 GB `bytes payload` in a frame.
> **Impact:** prost decoder allocates; OOM.
> **Exploitability:** trivial.
> **Suggested fix direction:** wrap decode in a length-prefixed
> reader with a hard cap (e.g., 2 × LoRa MTU for a single frame;
> 1 MB for a batch frame), reject larger.

A peer that sends 4 GB of bytes claiming to be a TransportFrame
forces every receiving node to allocate that buffer before prost
even attempts to parse it. Parse failure is a DoS amplifier
because the allocation already happened.

The fix lives in `arxia-proto` so every transport binding
(`arxia-transport`, future LoRa / BLE / SMS adapters) inherits
the same protocol-level limit and the same validator.

## Fix

Add a new module `validation.rs` that exposes a pure-bytes
validator callable BEFORE `prost::Message::decode`:

```rust
pub const MAX_TRANSPORT_FRAME_BYTES: usize = 1_048_576; // 1 MiB

pub enum ProtoError {
    TransportFrameTooLarge { size: usize, max: usize },
}

pub fn validate_transport_frame_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ProtoError> {
    if bytes.len() > MAX_TRANSPORT_FRAME_BYTES {
        return Err(ProtoError::TransportFrameTooLarge {
            size: bytes.len(),
            max: MAX_TRANSPORT_FRAME_BYTES,
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

Re-exported at the crate root so callers do
`arxia_proto::validate_transport_frame_bytes(&bytes)?;` then
`arxia_proto::arxia::TransportFrame::decode(bytes)?`.

### Why pure-bytes validation

The existing build pipeline runs `prost-build` only when `protoc`
is locally available. Without `protoc` (the common case in CI
sandbox / contributor laptop), `arxia.rs` is a stub and no proto
types are compiled. A validator that operates on `&[u8]` works
regardless of protoc availability — it's the **transport layer's
guard**, not the **proto layer's guard**.

Once protoc / the prost-built types land, callers will pair this
validator with `prost::Message::decode` at every transport
ingress site. The validator is the cheapest possible OOM-vector
closure: a single `len()` comparison against the constant.

### Cap value (1 MiB)

Aligned with the audit's batch-frame ceiling. Rationale:
- The largest known single envelope is `NonceSyncResponse` capped
  at ~720 KB by commit 028 (10 000 entries × 72 B each).
- 1 MiB leaves comfortable headroom (≈300 KB) for any future
  envelope additions.
- 1 MiB is far below the 4 GB attack the audit describes — the
  OOM amplifier is closed.

A future per-link tightening (e.g. `MAX_LORA_FRAME_BYTES = 512`)
can be added on top of this protocol-level ceiling without
loosening the global guard.

## Tests added

8 new tests in `arxia_proto::validation::tests`:

- `test_max_transport_frame_bytes_constant` — pin the cap at
  1 MiB. Future revision must update both const and assertion.
- `test_validate_accepts_empty_frame` — boundary: empty slice.
- `test_validate_accepts_small_frame` — realistic 64-byte Ping.
- `test_validate_accepts_realistic_batch_frame` — 720 KB
  (NonceSyncResponse near commit 028's cap).
- `test_validate_accepts_at_max` — boundary: exactly 1 MiB
  (cap is INCLUSIVE — `>`, not `>=`).
- `test_validate_rejects_just_above_max` — off-by-one:
  MAX + 1 must reject.
- `test_validate_rejects_attacker_scale_frame` — **PRIMARY
  HIGH-010 PIN.** 10 MiB attacker payload (the audit cites 4 GB;
  10 MiB is tractable in test memory while still well above the
  cap).
- `test_proto_error_display_format` — Display surface.

`arxia-proto` had **0 tests** before this commit. Total:
0 → 8.

## Order dependency

Standalone. No dependency on commits 023-039. Apply on top of
`ddb728b` directly.

## Breaking change disclosure

**No breaking change.** The new module + symbols are entirely
additive:
- `validation` module (new, public)
- `MAX_TRANSPORT_FRAME_BYTES` constant
- `ProtoError` enum
- `validate_transport_frame_bytes` function

Workspace caller audit:
- 0 callers today. The intended consumer is a future
  `arxia-transport` ingress that sits between the wire bytes and
  `prost::Message::decode`. The validator is exposed and ready.

## Known limitations

- **Validator is purely length-based.** Prost's own decode will
  still produce its own errors on malformed bytes (proto-level
  field mismatch, invalid varints, etc.). This validator only
  closes the OOM amplifier — it does NOT replace prost's
  parse-time checks.
- **No per-link cap.** A future enhancement could add
  `MAX_LORA_FRAME_BYTES = 512` or similar for constrained-link
  per-frame caps. Out of scope for HIGH-010 which is about the
  protocol-level OOM ceiling.
- **Adoption follow-up.** This commit adds the validator;
  wiring it at every `prost::Message::decode` site in
  `arxia-transport` and future LoRa / BLE / SMS adapters is a
  separate commit. The validator is exposed; consumers will
  inherit the cap when they call it.
- **No fuzz harness.** Single-comparison validator;
  exhaustively covered by 6 boundary tests (empty, small,
  realistic, at-max, MAX+1, 10 MiB).
- **HIGH-011 (GossipEnvelope unknown oneof) is the natural next
  step.** It depends on the prost-generated `GossipEnvelope`
  type which requires protoc; queued as commit 041.

Refs: PHASE1_AUDIT_REPORT.md HIGH-010.

| Proposal state | Has cached audit | Button |
|---|---|---|
| Open | No | **Run audit** |
| Open | Yes | **Show audit** |
| Executed | No | hidden |
| Executed | Yes | **Show audit** (review post-execution) |

body:
## Summary

Pre-public OSS security hygiene, scoped down to one piece:

- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** — weekly version-update PRs for Go modules and for the GitHub Actions used in workflows.

## What this PR does NOT include (intentionally)

- **CodeQL workflow** — code scanning on private repos requires GitHub Advanced Security (paid). On public repos it's free. Plan: enable via **Settings → Code security → Code scanning → default setup** after the repo flips public; that gives you CodeQL with no workflow file. If more configuration is wanted later, the workflow form can come back as a follow-up.
- **`SECURITY.md`** — removed per request; can revisit as a separate change later if needed.
- **govulncheck in CI.** Locally, `govulncheck ./...` against current `main` flags **22 vulnerabilities** the code reaches into — mostly older `golang.org/x/*` and stdlib advisories that need dep bumps to clear. Adding govulncheck to CI today would land main on red. The right order is: merge this → enable repo-level Dependabot → let it open the bump PRs → fix any remaining vulns → then add govulncheck to CI in a follow-up so it stays green.

## Repo-level toggles to enable (UI, not code)

The dependabot.yml is inert until **Settings → Code security → Dependabot version updates** is on. Recommended toggles for the public flip:

- ✅ Dependency graph
- ✅ Automatic dependency submission
- ✅ Dependabot alerts
- ✅ Dependabot malware alerts
- ✅ Dependabot security updates *(opens CVE patch PRs automatically)*
- ✅ Grouped security updates *(one PR per ecosystem when multiple advisories drop simultaneously)*
- ✅ Dependabot version updates
- ❌ Dependabot on self-hosted runners
- ✅ Secret scanning + Push protection *(in the secret-scanning section)*
- ✅ Code scanning → default setup *(after the repo goes public; free for public repos)*

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge this PR.
- [ ] Enable the repo-level toggles above (Code scanning waits until after public).
- [ ] Wait one cycle; confirm Dependabot opens its first wave of PRs (Go modules + Actions).
- [ ] After dep bumps land, open a follow-up PR adding `govulncheck` to ci.yml. CI should stay green.

body: ## Summary - Adds `workflows/wave11-flat-layout-collapse/01-collapse-packages-into-src.ts`, a deterministic workflow that collapses the current npm-workspaces layout (`packages/{shared,runtime,product,cloud,local,cli}`) into a single sage-style `src/` tree with topical subfolders and a `src/surfaces/cli/` directory (room for future `slack/`, `web/`, `mac/`). - Drives the migration via TDD: a new `test/flat-layout-proof/` is authored first and runs **RED** on the current layout, the workflow performs the moves + import-rewrite codemod + config consolidation, and only then drives typecheck + full test suite + flat-layout proof to **GREEN** before sign-off. - Replaces (not silently deletes) the existing `test/package-proof/` — the old proof asserts the very layout we are removing, so the new flat-layout proof is its successor. - Layer boundaries are enforced by folder convention only (matching sage). No path aliases, no eslint boundaries plugin. ## Workflow shape DAG with deterministic gates between every agent step: 1. `preflight` — capture before-snapshot, source inventory, and config baselines; refuse if working tree is dirty or `src/` already exists. 2. `write-flat-layout-proof` (test-author) → `red-gate` — assert the new test runs RED and inverts exit code so a passing test here fails the workflow. 3. `write-migration-plan` (migrator) → `plan-gate` — produce a TSV file map; gate verifies every source from the inventory has a destination row. 4. `execute-migration` (migrator) → `migration-structural-gate` — moves via `git mv`, recorded codemod for `@ricky/*` → relative imports, single root `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`/`vitest.config.ts`, deletes `packages/` and `test/package-proof/`, regenerates lockfile. 5. `green-validation` → `fix-loop` (fix) → `green-gate` — 80→100 loop until typecheck + `npm test` + flat-layout proof all exit 0 together. 6. `final-review` (reviewer) → `final-review-pass-gate` → `final-hard-validation` → `signoff`. ## Why a workflow and not a hand migration - Reproducibility: the codemod for the import rewrites is committed to `${artifactDir}/codemod.{mjs,ts}`, so the rewrite is auditable. - Safety: each gate is deterministic; nothing relies on agent self-report. - TDD discipline: the contract for "what flat looks like" lives in the test, not in the workflow prose — so the test survives as the long-term layout proof after the workflow run. ## Test plan - [ ] Code review of the workflow file against `workflows/shared/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING_RULES.md` and `docs/workflows/WORKFLOW_STANDARDS.md`. - [ ] Dry-run: `agent-relay run workflows/wave11-flat-layout-collapse/01-collapse-packages-into-src.ts --dry-run` (or repo-equivalent) to validate step graph and shell expansions. - [ ] On a throwaway branch, run the full workflow and confirm: `src/{shared,runtime,product,cloud,local,surfaces/cli}` populated, `packages/` removed, `test/package-proof/` removed, `test/flat-layout-proof/` present, `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm test` clean, `node bin/ricky --help` works. - [ ] Verify no `@ricky/*` import or `file:../` dep remains in the resulting tree. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

author: kevinguitar
body:
This PR adds a compiler test for generating providers in a generated dependency graph. 
~This PR supports FIR-generated providers to be processed in a generated dependency graph.~

Previously, when you added a provider in a generated graph:
```kotlin
@DependencyGraph
interface FeatureGraph {
  @Provides
  fun provideParam(): String = "foo"
}
```
the compilation would fail with this error:
```
No expected factory class generated for /MyActivity.FeatureGraph.provideParam. Report this bug with a repro case at https://github.com/zacsweers/metro/issues/new. This is possibly a bug in the Metro compiler, please report it with details and/or a reproducer to https://github.com/zacsweers/metro.
org.jetbrains.kotlin.fir.pipeline.IrGenerationExtensionException: No expected factory class generated for /MyActivity.FeatureGraph.provideParam. Report this bug with a repro case at https://github.com/zacsweers/metro/issues/new. This is possibly a bug in the Metro compiler, please report it with details and/or a reproducer to https://github.com/zacsweers/metro.
```
**Edit**: Annotated the dependency graph with `@IROnlyFactories` resolves the issue.

~and this is because when a `@Provides` function is generated by a FIR extension, it's generated at a phase after Metro's `ProvidesFactoryFirGenerator` has already looked at the `classSymbol.declarationSymbols` (is this expected?!) to find provider functions and generate corresponding factory classes.~

~Generating the factory in IR phase (`BindingContainerTransformer`) resolves the issue.~

body: ## Summary Stacks on PRs #1–#5. Gets the backend production-deployable on Fly.io with managed Postgres and tightens the parent-side auth surface. ### Auth hardening - Refresh tokens are now persisted to the existing `RefreshToken` model (sha256-hashed at rest). `/auth/refresh` **rotates**: it issues a new refresh + access pair and revokes the old refresh atomically. Reusing a revoked refresh token is treated as theft and revokes every refresh in that parent's chain. - `/auth/logout` revokes the presented refresh token. - `/auth/password-reset/request` + `/auth/password-reset/confirm` — 30-minute one-shot tokens stored as `PasswordResetToken` (sha256-hashed). Request endpoint always 200's to avoid email enumeration. The reset URL is logged via the notifier console adapter; replace `sendEmail` in `notifier.ts` to dispatch real emails. - `express-rate-limit` on `/auth/register`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/password-reset/request` with deterrent windows (10/hr register, 20/15min login, 5/hr reset). - `app.set("trust proxy", 1)` enabled when `NODE_ENV=production` or `TRUST_PROXY=1` so rate limits and `req.ip` see the real client behind Fly's edge. ### Parent UI - `/audit` — paginated audit log using cursor pagination over `GET /api/audit`. - `/password-reset` (request form) and `/password-reset/confirm` (set-new-password form, accepts `?token=` query). - "Forgot password?" link on the login page. - "Audit" link added to the header alongside "Notifications". ### Deploy infrastructure - `apps/backend/Dockerfile` — multi-stage (deps → build → prod). Uses pnpm workspaces, builds `@getkids/shared` and `@getkids/backend`, ships production deps only. ~150 MB image. - `apps/backend/scripts/start.sh` runs `prisma migrate deploy` and then `node dist/index.js` so the first deploy auto-applies migrations against Fly Postgres. - `apps/backend/fly.toml` — `sin` region (Singapore, closest to target users in Indonesia), `/health` HTTP check, auto-stop machines, `min_machines_running=1`. - `docs/DEPLOY.md` — end-to-end runbook covering the SQLite → Postgres provider switch, Fly app + Postgres provisioning, secret setup, web app static hosting (Vercel/Netlify), notification provider wiring, signed Android release. - `.dockerignore` to keep dev artifacts out of the build context. The dev schema stays on SQLite (`provider = "sqlite"`) for local convenience. DEPLOY.md walks through the two-line provider switch + migration rebaseline before first prod deploy. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Refresh rotation** — login, copy refresh token, hit `/auth/refresh`, confirm response includes a *new* refresh token. Try `/auth/refresh` again with the *old* token — should 401 `refresh_reuse_detected`. Confirm all that parent's refresh tokens are now revoked in the DB. - [ ] **Password reset** — `POST /auth/password-reset/request {email}` → check backend stdout for `[auth:password-reset] parent=... token=...`. Hit `/password-reset/confirm` with that token + new password → 200. Try logging in with the old password → 401. Try the reset token a second time → `invalid_or_expired`. - [ ] **Rate limits** — fire 30 `POST /auth/login` from one IP; confirm a `429` after limit. Try the same from a different IP via header rewrite (after `TRUST_PROXY=1`); confirm independent counter. - [ ] **Audit page** — make a few policy edits and command actions, confirm `/audit` shows them with newest first. - [ ] **Docker build** — `docker build -f apps/backend/Dockerfile -t getkids-backend .` succeeds locally. ### Notes - This PR does NOT switch the dev schema to Postgres; the steps to do so are in `docs/DEPLOY.md`. Doing it inline would force every dev to install Postgres before working on unrelated tasks. - Push token registration (FCM `device.fcmToken`) is documented but intentionally left for the same future PR that wires real provider keys — without a Firebase project ID, the registration is just dead code. - 2FA TOTP isn't in this PR. It's a meaningful addition but doubles the surface area; happy to do it as a follow-up if you want. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/82d5957c75884e51881e6a6ebdeb7e08 Requested by: @groxce ---

First of two PRs that lift parsedmarc's mailbox abstraction into mailsuite so applications can read/manage mail across multiple providers behind one interface. After both land, parsedmarc consumes mailsuite for this layer instead of maintaining its own copy.

This PR merges the Phase 6/7 UI work and AI Advisor features back into main. The branch already absorbed the latest main (V2            
  forecasting, DB layer, deploy infra) through a per-file conflict resolution merge, so this is a clean fast-forward. 21 files changed,   
  +3,007 / −452.                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                          
  **What's new on the backend**                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                          
  - Phase 6A staleness reconciliation in api.py — when PortWatch data is stale but live AIS coverage is trustworthy, the displayed        
  congestion tier gets bumped up without modifying the underlying score.                                                                  
  - Phase 6A.2 spatial coverage classification — every port is tagged covered, sparse, dark, or unavailable based on nearby AIS vessel    
  counts. The UI uses this to show "Limited live coverage" or "Live coverage unavailable" warnings instead of pretending stale numbers are
   fresh. 
  - Three new ranking endpoints: /api/top-ports (most anomalous, z-score based), /api/top-loaded-ports (highest absolute portcalls), and  
  /api/coverage-snapshot.                                                                                                                 
  - AI Advisor robustness fix in llm.py — answer_text now initializes to None instead of raw, killing the JSON-leak bug that occasionally 
  surfaced in chat replies.                                                                                                               
  - Four new advisor endpoints: /api/advisor/briefing (auto-generated daily insights), /api/advisor/scenario (preset disruption 
  simulations), /api/advisor/compare (multi-port comparison), /api/advisor/nearby-ports.                                                  
  - New port_profiles.json with 25 port profiles for the port-click info panel.
  - New port_anchor_thresholds.py with per-port anchored/moored thresholds for vessel status classification.                              
                                                                                                                                          
  **What's new on the frontend**                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                          
  - Light/dark theme toggle with localStorage persistence — implemented as CSS custom properties so existing components didn't need       
  restyling.                           
  - Most Anomalous Ports + Most Loaded Ports — the left sidebar now shows two ranked lists instead of one ambiguous "Port Availability"   
  list. They answer different questions: which ports are having unusual days vs which ports are simply busiest right now.                 
  - Phase 6A.2 data freshness indicators on the port hero card — sparse/dark/unavailable badges on top of the existing "Xd behind
  real-time" line.

  - Cached divIcon factories for map markers (sonar pulse and port-center anchor), keyed by congestion tier — avoids icon-thrashing on    
  every render.                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                          
  **Conflict resolutions during the merge**                                                                                               
                                       
  Three files conflicted and were resolved by hand:                                                                                       
   
  - data_cleaning.py — kept the DATABASE_URL gate with absolute CSV fallback path, adopted low_memory=False from V2.

  port's detail view.

## Summary

Review follow-up #1 (BLOCKING) from `docs/handoff-prompts/voog-mcp-review-followups.md`.

`voog_mcp/errors.py:7` returned `list[TextContent]`, which the MCP SDK's `Server.call_tool()` decorator wraps as `CallToolResult(isError=False)`. Per spec § 7 (`docs/specs/2026-04-26-mcp-server.md`), every tool error must surface as `isError=True` content blocks so clients (Claude included) can distinguish a tool-level failure from a successful response. As-is, both paths looked identical on the wire.

Verified the SDK behaviour locally:

```
.venv/bin/python -c "import inspect; from mcp.server.lowlevel.server import Server; print(inspect.getsource(Server.call_tool))"
```

— the handler short-circuits with `if isinstance(results, types.CallToolResult): return ServerResult(results)`, so a fully-formed `CallToolResult` from us is passed through untouched.

## What changed

- `voog_mcp/errors.py`: `error_response()` now returns `CallToolResult(content=[…], isError=True)`. `success_response()` stays as `list[TextContent]` — the SDK's default `isError=False` wrapping is correct for that path.
- `voog_mcp/tools/*.py` (8 files): return-type annotations updated to `list[TextContent] | CallToolResult` on the public `call_tool` and on every internal `_*` helper that propagates `error_response()`.
- Tests (`tests/test_errors.py` + 8 `tests/test_tools_*.py`): error-path assertions migrated from `result[0].text` to `result.content[0].text`, with an explicit `assertTrue(result.isError)` so the spec contract is asserted, not just the payload shape.
- New unit test in `tests/test_errors.py` asserts the type/shape contract directly: `error_response` is a `CallToolResult` with `isError=True`; `success_response` is `list[TextContent]`.
- New integration test in `tests/test_mcp_integration.py::TestMCPInitialize::test_tool_validation_error_returns_iserror_true`: end-to-end check that calls `page_delete` without `force=true` over the JSON-RPC transport (dummy token, no live API) and asserts `result.isError == True` plus the expected `force=true` error message.

## Verification

```
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover tests
# 393 tests pass (was 392) — net +1 from the new integration test;
# the new unit test in test_errors.py replaces an existing one in place,
# so the unit count is unchanged.
```

- [x] New integration test (test_mcp_integration.py) asserts `isError=True` on the wire for a tool-validation failure

author: yuume2
body:
## Summary

Five-commit batch hardening the `/v1/messages/stream` SSE endpoint. The headline change is a real production bug fix: provider streams kept billing tokens after the client disconnected, because Node's `IncomingMessage` 'close' event doesn't fire reliably on socket teardown once the request body has been fully consumed.

### Commits

1. **`flushHeaders`** — ship SSE `Content-Type` + `X-Accel-Buffering: no` immediately so reverse proxies / browsers see them before the first delta, instead of letting Node buffer the response start until enough body is queued.
2. **`[DONE]` is last on success** — regression test locking that `[DONE]` is the final SSE sentinel emitted on the happy path. Anything after it is silently dropped by clients.
3. **`[DONE]` is last on error** — same guarantee on the provider-throws-mid-stream catch path. Without it, error-recovering clients hang on the read loop.
4. **Listen on `res`, not `req`, for client disconnect** — the production fix. Switches `ctx.req.on('close')` → `res.on('close')` (gated on `!res.writableEnded` so `res.end()` from normal completion doesn't trigger the abort path). Adds a regression test that parks the upstream generator on the abort signal and asserts it flips within the test budget — proves the cancel chain reaches the provider in production-equivalent conditions.
5. **Swallow `res 'error'`** — a mid-stream socket error (ECONNRESET, EPIPE) emits 'error' on the ServerResponse. With no listener, Node escalates it to unhandled and the API process can crash. Treat it like a client disconnect: cancel upstream and let the for-await throw exit cleanly.

### Why this matters

Before commit 4, the controller already threaded an `AbortSignal` through to each provider (merged in #135), but the signal never aborted in practice because the close detection was on the wrong event source. Paid OpenAI / Anthropic / Perplexity streams kept running and billing until they completed naturally.

Load Config from a file called config.json on boot. Create it if it doesn't exist, using existing defaults.

Create a ButtonPin class and use this to configure the ButtonDef with the hardware source and pin. This allows us to load the config and read the device and pin matching each button from config, meaning each saxophone build can have its own button to pin mapping.

Finally, in order to write to the filesystem from the circuitpython code, we have to do this hack to storage. The storage can only be writable by the saxophone or your computer when plugged in, but not both.  boot.py makes this work:

1. by default only the saxophone code can write to storage. This allows it to write config.json as needed. It also means when you plug the saxophone into a computer it will be read-only.
2. to write from your computer, you must hold down any two buttons on the right hand keys while plugging in the device, and it must be powered off before plugging in. in this mode, the saxophone will not be able to write config.json but will be able to read config.

author: chen3feng
body:
## Summary

The `Sanitizers (ubuntu-latest)` job finally told us the real story: the
non-MSVC CI failure is **not** a GCC/Clang miscompile of `BitCopyFast.cpp`.
It is a dangling-reference bug in our own CI shim, `CI/ue_shim.h`, that
happened to be invisible at `-O0` and loud at `-O2`.

AddressSanitizer report (from the last failing run on `main`):

```
==2344==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-use-after-return on address 0x7fceec600030
    #0 BitsCopyFastUnaligned  Source/FastBitCopy/Private/BitCopyFast.cpp:183
    #1 appBitsCpyFastImpl     Source/FastBitCopy/Private/BitCopyFast.cpp:352
    #2 main                   CI/test_main.cpp:249

Address 0x7fceec600030 is located in stack of thread T0 at offset 48 in frame
    #0 FMath::Min<int,int>(int, int)   CI/ue_shim.h:52
  This frame has 2 object(s):
    [48, 52) 'a' (line 52) <== Memory access at offset 48 is inside this variable
```

The memory being read by `BitsCopyFastUnaligned` at line 183 belongs to
`FMath::Min`'s own stack frame, specifically parameter `a`. That only
makes sense if `Min` was returning a reference to `a`, not a copy.

## Root cause

```cpp
template <class A, class B>
static constexpr auto Min(A a, B b) -> decltype(a < b ? a : b)
{
    return a < b ? a : b;
}
```

`decltype(a < b ? a : b)` where `a` and `b` are same-typed **lvalues**
evaluates to an **lvalue reference type** (`int&`). So the trailing
return type is `int&`, and `Min` returns a reference to its
by-value parameter -- a dangling reference the moment `Min` returns.

Why it stayed hidden:

* **`-O2`**: the caller (`BitsCopyFastUnaligned`) has `const int CopyBits
  = FMath::Min(CopySrcBits, BitCount);`. The compiler materialises
  `CopyBits` by reading from the returned reference slot *after* `Min`
  has returned, by which time the stack has been reused. That is the
  UB. ASan's `detect_stack_use_after_return=1` (default on this
  toolchain) is what made it a deterministic error.
* **`-O0`**: no stack reuse, the dead slot still had the correct value,
  so the job kept passing. That is why every `Standalone test -O0` run
  was green and we kept (wrongly) concluding that the helpers
  themselves needed to be pinned to `-O0`.
* **MSVC**: different codegen for same-type `?:` + different stack
  layout meant the read happened to still be valid.

Essentially every "fix" we tried on `BitCopyFast.cpp` itself --
`optnone`, `noinline`, `asm ("" ::: "memory")` barriers, forcing
`uint32` intermediates for the shifts -- was treating a symptom of a
bug that lives two files away.

## Fix

Return by value, matching UE's real `FMath::Min<T>(T, T)`:

```cpp
template <class T>
static constexpr T Min(T a, T b) { return a < b ? a : b; }
template <class T>
static constexpr T Max(T a, T b) { return a > b ? a : b; }
```

`BitCopyFast.cpp` only ever calls `FMath::Min(int, int)` /
`FMath::Max(int, int)`, so collapsing the two template parameters into
one `T` is safe. The shim is only used by the standalone CI harness;
the in-engine plugin build links against real UE `FMath` and was
never affected.

## Verification (actual CI on this branch)

| Job | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone test **(ubuntu-latest, -O2)** | :x: | :white_check_mark: |
| Standalone test **(macos-latest, -O2)**  | :x: | :white_check_mark: |
| Standalone test (windows-latest, MSVC)   | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| Standalone test -O0 (ubuntu / macos)     | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| arm64 cross-build (linux)                | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| Dump -O2 assembly (linux)                | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| Validate .uplugin                        | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| **Sanitizers (ubuntu-latest)**           | :x: (SUAR)        | :x: (*different* bug -- see below) |

The `-O2` functional failures on Linux and macOS -- the entire
motivation for this PR -- are **fixed**.

## What remains red and why I am *not* fixing it in this PR

The `Sanitizers` job is still red, but with a completely different
error that only became reachable once we stopped crashing on the
stack-use-after-return:

```
BitCopyFast.cpp:133:20: runtime error: load of misaligned address
0x521000000101 for type 'long unsigned int', which requires 8 byte alignment
```

Line 133 is `const WordType Word = Src[i];`, i.e. dereferencing a
`uint64*` that was cast from `uint8*` at an arbitrary byte offset.
On x86/x64 the hardware is happy to do this (that is exactly what
`PLATFORM_SUPPORTS_UNALIGNED_LOADS=1` promises), so the code is
*functionally* correct -- which is why every non-sanitized job is
now green. But it is language-level UB according to C++, and UBSan
with `-fsanitize=alignment` (on by default in the Sanitizers job) is
specifically there to catch exactly this.

This is a pre-existing issue, not regressed by this PR. It was
simply masked before: the earlier stack-use-after-return aborted the
sanitized run inside `BitsCopyFastUnaligned` long before execution
ever reached this aligned-path load. Now that the crash is gone,
UBSan runs further and surfaces the next latent issue.

I am keeping it out of this PR deliberately, because:

1. It is a different class of bug (language-level alignment UB vs
   lifetime UB).
2. The fix touches production code (`BitCopyFast.cpp`), not the
   test shim, so the reviewer's attention should be separate.
3. This PR's claim -- "fix the `-O2` Linux/macOS failures" -- is
   already fully substantiated by the table above, and inflating
   scope would muddy the bisect story.

## Follow-ups (tracked separately, not in this PR)

1. `BitCopyFast.cpp`: replace raw `uint64*` dereferences with
   `std::memcpy`-based reads/writes so the code is both
   language-legal and optimal (Clang/GCC collapse `memcpy(&w,p,8)`
   to a single load). Closes the Sanitizers alignment warning.
2. `BitCopyFast.cpp`: revert the defensive noise accumulated while
   we were chasing the wrong bug -- `optimize("O0")` /
   `__attribute__((optnone))` / `asm ("" ::: "memory")` barriers /
   manual `uint32` promotions for the shift chain. None of it was
   needed; it was all treating symptoms of the shim bug.
3. `FastBitCopyModule.cpp`: re-enable the hook on non-MSVC builds
   (we disabled it defensively while fallback was believed
   necessary; now that the helpers are provably correct, the hook
   can go back on).
4. `README.md`: drop the "Linux / macOS: partial" language and
   close #2.
5. `agent-skills`: record the lesson
   (`decltype(cond ? a : b)` on same-typed lvalues yields
   `T&`; never use it as a trailing return type for a function
   that took its operands by value).

## Summary

Hotfix for user-reported \"map oversized in the canvas\" on `/explore/emotion-pulse/`.

## Root cause

After the Phase 3a fit-iframe hotfix (#78) made `.plot-wrap` fill 100% of the iframe, Plotly rendered the chart at the full iframe height — which is `desktop_height: 1100` from `data/canonical.json`.
